canonical_answers: ∮B·dl=B(2πr)=μ₀I, so B=μ₀I/(2πr) in the azimuthal direction.

payload.text: A long straight wire carries current I along +z; find the field using a circular Amperian loop of radius r.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Design a feasible measurement that tests the governing relation; identify the independent variable, dependent variable, and one control.

criteria.description: A valid design varies the current I as the independent variable, measures the resulting magnetic field B at a fixed radius r as the dependent variable, and holds the radial distance r (and probe position along the wire) constant as the control, consistent with B=μ₀I/(2πr).
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.
criteria.minimum_fix: To earn this point, explicitly show independent variable: current I; dependent variable: measured field B; control: fixed radius r.

parts.prompt: State the governing principle (Ampere's law) and the assumption of cylindrical symmetry about the wire, and explain why each is required for the proposed measurement of B(r) to be valid.
